root.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: Vitolins Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 c5

overview: Black meets 4.Bd2 with 4...c5, so after 5.Bxb4 cxb4 White usually continues with 6.g3 and a kingside fianchetto. White has more space in the centre with c4 and d4, and Black has an advanced b4 pawn and play against the c- and e-pawns. It is balanced and slightly unusual, and Black can choose between ...Bb7 and ...Qb6.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, then castle and play for the centre
Use the c- and d-pawns for a space advantage

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Bb7 and ...O-O, with pressure against the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: White c4/d4 pawns against Black b4/e6 pawns
Flexible pawn tension in the centre

character.notes: A positional struggle over the centre and the b4 pawn, neither solid nor sharp.

gambit.notes: Pieces are traded and no material is offered.

soundness.notes: Fully playable at high level for both sides.

structure.notes: The tension between c4/d4 and the ...c5 pawn leaves the centre undecided.

approach.notes: Respectable and played by strong players, though not the main line.

character.reason: The game is a positional fight without forcing lines or an especially safe set-up.

structure.reason: The c4/d4 centre faces ...c5 and ...d6 breaks and is not locked.

approach.reason: A respectable choice for strong players.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and holds more space in the centre.
